transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you and what brings you in today?

I guess… I just haven’t been quite myself since a friend from choir passed away suddenly. Little things at church, like potluck lists or phone calls I used to handle fine, have been getting me all worked up. I’ve even missed a few planning things, which isn’t like me.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like choir or other church activities?

A little, I suppose. Since my choir friend passed so suddenly, I just… haven’t felt like myself. Choir and church things still matter to me, but I get upset over small things now, like potluck lists or making calls, and I’ve missed some planning things I normally wouldn’t.
Have you found that you don’t take as much pleasure in choir or other church activities as you used to?
I’m… not really sure. I still go, and it still feels important to me. Maybe it’s not quite the same lately, but I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped caring about it.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting as much enjoyment out of choir or other church activities as you used to?
I don’t know… maybe a little, but I still go. I wouldn’t say I don’t enjoy it at all. It just feels different lately, I suppose.
Would you say that you’re taking less pleasure in choir or church activities than you used to, or do they still feel about the same to you?
I’m not sure I can say. They still matter to me, and I still go. It’s just… not quite as easy lately, I guess.
Would you say that you take less pleasure in most of your usual activities, not just choir or church things, compared to before your friend passed away?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about it that way. Things feel… different since then, but I don’t know if I’d say I take less pleasure in most things.
Would you say that you've been feeling down or sad most of the day, nearly every day, since your friend passed away?
I don’t know… I’ve had sad days, sure. But most of the day, nearly every day? I’m not sure I’d put it that way.
Would you say that you've been feeling down or sad most of the day, nearly every day, since your friend passed away?

I don’t know if it’s most of the day every day… but since she passed so suddenly, I just haven’t felt like myself. Little things set me off now, even church planning calls or potluck lists. I get upset over things I used to handle fine.
Would you say that you find yourself preoccupied with thoughts about your friend who passed away, or have difficulty accepting what happened?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I think about her sometimes, of course… but I don’t know if I’d call it preoccupied. And accepting it… I mean, it’s hard, but I haven’t really sorted that out.
Have you found yourself feeling anxious, worried, or on edge about things more than usual since your friend passed away?

Yes… I guess more than usual. Since my choir friend died so suddenly, I get worked up over things I used to handle fine—calls, potluck lists, church planning. I’ve even missed some things I normally wouldn’t.
Have you found yourself worrying a lot or feeling overly concerned about things related to your friend’s passing or other church responsibilities since this happened?

Yes… I suppose I have. Ever since she passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. I get worked up over church calls and potluck lists—things I used to manage fine—and I’ve even missed some planning things I wouldn’t have before.
Have you found yourself feeling restless, keyed up, or on edge even when there’s no specific church task or worry about your friend on your mind?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. If there isn’t something I’m dealing with, I don’t think I’m just sitting there keyed up. At least I haven’t noticed that.
Have you noticed any physical changes, like trouble sleeping, fatigue, or muscle tension, since your friend passed away?
I’m not sure… I haven’t really noticed anything like that in particular. Maybe I’m a bit tired sometimes, but I couldn’t say it’s changed much.
Have you noticed yourself feeling anxious or uneasy even when there’s nothing specific you need to do or worry about since your friend passed away?
I don’t think so… not just out of nowhere. It’s more when something reminds me of it, or there’s something I’m supposed to handle. Otherwise, I haven’t really noticed that.
Would you say that you feel anxious or worried even when there’s nothing specific on your mind or no immediate task to handle?
No… I don’t think so. If nothing’s really on my mind, I’m usually not worrying. At least, I haven’t noticed it that way.
Would you say that you worry about things even when they’re not directly related to church responsibilities or your friend’s passing?
Not really… I don’t think I worry much outside of those things. If it’s not connected to that, I usually don’t dwell on it.
Would you say that you worry about things even when they’re not connected to church or your friend’s passing, like everyday matters that wouldn’t usually bother you?
I haven’t really noticed that, no. Everyday things… they don’t usually get to me unless they somehow tie back to all of that.
Would you say that you worry about things that aren’t related to church or your friend’s passing, like regular everyday tasks or responsibilities that didn’t used to bother you?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, regular things are still just regular things. I haven’t really noticed myself worrying about them more than before.
Would you say that you feel anxious or worry about things even when they’re not connected to anything specific like church or your friend’s passing, and just seem to come up on their own?
I don’t think so… not just out of nowhere. It mostly seems tied to what’s been going on.
